capabilities: Application lifecycle: owned initial state, schema registration, text mount/dispose (implemented A.1)
Copy-on-write transactions, rollback, stable identity and growth guards (implemented A.2)
Named actions, owned validated payloads and bounded FIFO dispatch (implemented A.3)
DOM-1: Declarative DOM abstraction (planned Phase A)
DOM-2: Fine-grained DOM updates (planned Phase A)
STATE-1: Deep reactive store (planned Phase A)
ACTION-1: Synchronous transactional named actions (implemented A.3; reactive observers follow A.4)
EVENT-1: Framework event system (planned Phase B)
TIME-1: Deterministic simulation ticks (planned Phase C)
RECORD-1: Action recording & replay (planned Phase C)

results.name: default mount resolves #app only at mount time and preserves host children
missing default target fails before view invocation and retries when #app appears
explicit invalid/custom targets never silently use available #app
default mount preserves exclusive ownership and lifecycle errors without a target
public browser-native module exports current lifecycle metadata
lazy create, explicit mount, terminal/idempotent dispose
configured target mounts automatically with immutable context
owned initial state is deep read-only without freezing caller data
aliases, holes and null prototypes preserve meaning in native JS
dynamic text cannot inject HTML
host children, native focus and selection survive mount/dispose
target claim is exclusive and released after disposal
invalid DOM-like targets/documents/shadow roots reject
same app cannot double-mount or move to another target
failed view unwinds its scope and permits retry on the same target
cleanup is reverse-order and repeated disposal does not rerun it
cleanup errors do not block later cleanup/DOM removal/claim release
owned node removal follows a moved node but does not remove unrelated nodes
registered action wrappers execute synchronous commits and names are owned
schema shared by apps does not share stores or disposal
public action rollback preserves committed snapshots, text, native focus and selection
public payload admission copies aliases and sparse arrays without invoking unsupported getters
public FIFO dispatch commits parent before children and runs grandchildren after siblings
failed public children discard descendants, continue siblings and report after draining
public illegal async actions reject atomically and revoke post-await mutation
public self-dispatch has a batch bound and recovers for a later call
view mutation fails before publishing text
Promise-returning views reject with cleanup and no unhandled native rejection
DOM state and unsupported Array prototypes reject
iframe DOM targets work while foreign-realm state is not normalized
detached DOM targets can mount and dispose without a connected page
A.2 transactions publish atomically and throwing bodies roll back
A.2 aliases, moved item identity and untouched branches survive native array operations
A.2 committed metadata is exact and freezes supported data
A.2 successful no-op advances a version and native revocation also blocks reflection
A.2 array and depth growth limits reject without partial publication
A.2 illegal native async work is rejected and its late draft mutation is observed
100 cycles return owned nodes, cleanup counts and target claims to baseline
root public-import example uses default mount and public disposal without DOM patching

limitations: Public lifecycle/text-only views, named dispatch and internal COW engine; no events/reactivity/replay or cross-browser/IME qualification. Resource counters are not a heap-leak proof.
